lens: Red-team architect and user advocate: over-engineering, departures from the user's literal spec, and a simpler path to first use

issues.section: §10 'Good enough to start using' (v1 definition of done, line ~513); §11 Roadmap v1 column; §1 repository layout
issues.problem: First use is gated on the entire v1 column, so the user's explicit priority (use it soon) waits for features the walkthrough never touches. The column lists about 20 deliverables: CLI export/check/init/fmt, Lean-editor providers, DECISION records, sign-off with back-translation, Instruct, two-phase runs, gate G0–G6, Playwright plus vscode-test integration tests, and the monorepo layout (core, extension, webview, cli, plus lean/TeleleanTools).
issues.evidence: §10: 'everything in the v1 column below works on mental_model/, all automated tests pass, and the manual Claude walkthrough succeeds end to end.' S9: 'because I want to use this'. S52: 'let me know when it is in a state that is good enough for me to start using it'. D-31 even puts a sudo install (xvfb) on the path. None of the CLI, providers, DECISION records, back-translation, Instruct, comparator or vscode-test are needed for S17–S33.
issues.suggested_fix: Define a v0.1 'walkthrough-usable' milestone and make that the point you report as 'good enough to start using'. It contains: markup in the user's syntax; the 3-column board (aura, status, selection tray, drag); the A/D/G prompt box; a semantic refresh of lake build plus one generated check file; ClaudeCliBackend (or the SDK backend) plus FakeBackend; one-shot Prove-from-selection; Formalize-only; questions; gate G0–G3 plus a G5 subset; proposal overlay plus raw diff; accept/feedback/discard; and .telelean/graph.json. Keep it to one package and one Model.lean file. Support a single Lake root, with a setting to choose it. On a diverged accept, refuse and offer re-run or resume with the diff instead of a three-way merge. Tests: vitest on the core, Lean 4.35 fixtures in which every exploit is rejected, a FakeBackend controller test of S18–S33, and one manual Claude run. List the rest as v0.2+ increments for the user to prioritise.

issues.section: D-18 ★ (two-phase run); also 03 §8.3 propose_formalization, §8.4 Freeze, §8.5 G4, §14
issues.problem: Two-phase runs replace S31/S33's single 'propose a diff when done, accept or give feedback' with two checkpoints. They also add a blocking sign-off UI, a leanexport freeze, a generated comparator.json, frozen state under .telelean/frozen, and a separate back-translation session on every run. This duplicates the design's own Formalize-only action, which already gives a statements-first flow when the user wants one.
issues.evidence:
S31: 'When the LLM is done, it will propose a diff'. R5 itself lists one-shot as the 'simpler' alternative. R5 measured the frozen export at 18,538 lines for the toy model. The comparator's permitted-axiom check would reject sorry'd statements unless they are excluded from theorem_names (inferred from `lake help comparator`). The independent back-translation is a second session per run, which costs subscription usage.

Experiment (Lean 4.35.0, scratch project): `set_option pp.all true` with `#check @X` prints a canonical, fully qualified, notation-free statement in 0.42 s and 472 MB RSS. Comparing that string between the base and the proposal mechanically detects changes to statements that were already accepted. That is the only freeze that one-shot runs need.
issues.suggested_fix: Make one-shot the default. In the final diff, list every new or changed formal statement, and every bodied definition on a statement or proof path, as a 'You said / Lean says' row. Show the source text, with a pp.all notation-free toggle, and require each row to be ticked before Accept is enabled. Place these rows above proof status to reduce automation bias. Offer 'Formalize first' (the existing Formalize-only action) and a setting 'review statements before proving' for users who want two phases. Replace G4 with the 'accepted statements unchanged' check described in the evidence, and flag any changed declaration those statements mention. Move the independent back-translation to an opt-in in v1.x.

issues.evidence:
R7: 'Run the user's installed Claude Code CLI as learnharness does … --tools "" --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config … --permission-prompts none'. Its tools are served from a loopback Streamable-HTTP MCP server with a bearer token, so no separate MCP process and no control protocol are needed. R6: 'Direct spawning has fewer moving parts'.

R1's objection (the control protocol must be hand-implemented) applies only if canUseTool, hooks or in-process MCP are used. R5's objection (a separate stdio MCP process) does not apply to an in-host HTTP server.

The saved `claude --help` for 2.1.314 documents `--restricted`: it removes the built-in tools that run commands or code, ignores user, project and local settings files, and confines the file tools to the working directories. That is the path guard plus `settingSources: []` as one flag. It also documents `--tools`, `--input-format stream-json`, `--resume` and `--permission-prompts none`.

R1: 'Nothing was run against a live login or API because node is not installed', so the SDK route has never been exercised. The CLI route can be smoke-tested from a shell today, with no Node needed.

issues.section: D-3 ★, D-4 ★, D-19 (not ★); 03 §2.1 NodeKind, §3.2 fields, §3.3 DECISION example, §4 table
issues.problem: The user specified three kinds and three sections; the schema in their Lean files grows to five kinds. DECISION, a `kind: DECISION` block in Model/Decisions.lean, is an unstarred default, so it would be built without the user being asked. DEFINITION is not needed as a markup kind either: D-3 places vocabulary at the top of the ASSUMPTIONS column, and §4 encodes it as `axiom T : Type`, which is literally 'an axiom' (S5).
issues.evidence:
03 §2.1: `type NodeKind = 'ASSUMPTION' | 'DERIVATION' | 'GOAL' | 'DEFINITION' | 'DECISION'`. 02 preamble: 'Everything else is a default I will apply unless you object', and D-19 is not ★. S4 and S11–S14 name exactly three kinds and sections.

Experiment: `example : Prop := type_of% @X` elaborates exactly when axiom X is Prop-valued. It errors on `HasDarkPast : Character → Prop` and `cynder : Character` and succeeds on `cynder_dark_past` and `pg_no_dark_past` (0.44 s, no `import Lean`). So the vocabulary-versus-belief role can be computed from Lean rather than declared.
issues.suggested_fix:
Keep `type:` ∈ {ASSUMPTION, DERIVATION, GOAL}. Treat vocabulary as ASSUMPTION-column items whose bound declarations are Type-valued axioms, structures or inductives, a role computed from Lean, and show them as the collapsed box-card group D-3 already proposes. Keep D-4's protection as computed rows in the final review: bodied definitions on a statement or proof path must be ticked before Accept.

Make DECISION a ★ question. For v0.1, keep the questions and answers in .telelean/sessions/ and feed earlier answers into later runs as context. Promote them to first-class records only if the user wants that common ground in their Lean files.

issues.section: D-9 ★ (kind: replaces type:); 03 §3.1 marker rule, §3.2, §3.4 TL018
issues.problem: The design renames the one concrete field the user wrote (`type: GOAL`) for a taste reason, and makes the validator nag when the user writes it: TL018 says 'type: used; prefer kind:', and a missing version marker is v1 'with a hint'. The documents also disagree with each other about the field name.
issues.evidence: S37 uses `type: GOAL`. Doc 01 Appendix D item 10 resolves the schema with '`id`, `type`, `natural_name`…', and t1's resolution also uses `type`. R5's system-prompt skeleton writes `type: ASSUMPTION | DERIVATION | GOAL`. Doc 03 line 136: 'missing version = v1 (with a hint)'.
issues.suggested_fix: Make `type:` canonical, so the serializer writes `type:`. Accept `kind:` silently as an alias, drop TL018, and treat an absent version marker as v1 without a hint. The user is a Lean expert and chose `type:` knowingly.

issues.section: D-16 ★ (Instruct as 4th switch position); 03 §7 PromptBox, §8.4 heading, §8.5 G4
issues.problem: Instruct changes the user's three-position switch, and its verification policy is undefined. §8.4 says Formalize-only and Instruct reuse the button's pipeline. But G4's permitted axioms are defined by a selection, Instruct has none, and Formalize-only produces sorry'd theorems.
issues.evidence: S4: marked 'as either creating an ASSUMPTION, a DERIVATION or a GOAL'. 03 §8.5 G4: 'permitted_axioms = the 3 standard + vocabulary + the selected assumptions'. A comparator permitted-axiom check rejects sorryAx unless those theorems are excluded (inferred from `lake help comparator`).
issues.suggested_fix: Keep the switch at A|D|G exactly. Send free-form requests through the conversation strip, which already exists for answers and feedback. Define the policy explicitly: permitted axioms = all existing ASSUMPTIONs; the run may add only ghost assumptions and may not reclassify. Alternatively, defer Instruct past v0.1.

issues.problem: v1 depends on a compiled Lean extractor. It is a 231 MB binary built per toolchain on internal APIs that drift ('several renames were hit on 4.35'), plus a front-end mode for broken files. Everything v1 needs from it can be had from one generated check file. The documented fallback is the RAM-heavy path, which matters for a user whose machine has crashed from memory exhaustion.
issues.evidence:
Experiment in scratchpad/review/redteam/axp (Lean 4.35.0, toy Spyro model, one Lean process at a time):
- A Check.lean with no `open` prints fully qualified `#print axioms` lists, including sorryAx and propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound, via `lake env lean --json`. With `set_option pp.fullNames true` names stay qualified even under `open`. This refutes R5's 'namespace-relative, should not be parsed' for generated files.
- `type_of%` probes classify each axiom as Prop or vocabulary.
- pp.all `#check` gives canonical statements.
- Each run takes about 0.43 s wall and about 471 MB RSS, with no `import Lean`.
- A comparable interpreted `import Lean` script (collectAxioms plus getUsedConstants) took 1.60 s and 1.6 GB RSS, about 3× the extractor's documented 475 MB. The documented fallback ('lake env lean --run, about 3–5 s') imports Lean the same way (inferred).
- #print axioms and collectAxioms share the skipKernelTC blind spot, which G0 plus leanchecker cover in both designs.
issues.suggested_fix: For v0.1, the semantic layer is lake build plus one generated check file containing `#print axioms` with pp.fullNames for every bound declaration, `type_of%` probes for every axiom found, and pp.all `#check` for formal nodes, parsed from --json. Any name that does not resolve fails closed. Build the compiled extractor only when lemma-level dependency edges, type hashes or partial facts for broken files are needed. Correct §5 to say that the interpreted fallback costs about 1.6 GB RSS.

issues.section: §6 'Lean-editor providers'; §9 CLI; §11 v1 column; §6 settings telelean.docstringMirror (false); 02 D-28, D-10 ★
issues.problem: Having answered 'LSP: not now', v1 still builds the LSP feature set in process plus a five-command CLI with a JSON Schema. The user said they will mostly work in the panel, and scripts are a 'might'. Meanwhile the user's own suggestion for showing natural language in Lean, a docstring, is off by default, and a custom hover provider replaces it.
issues.evidence: §6 lists diagnostics, hover, completion, definition/references, rename, CodeLens, quick fixes and a TextMate injection grammar. §9 lists `export|check|init|fmt|schema`. S42: 'he is expected to mostly work in the extension window'. S43: 'we might also write separate scripts'. S40: 'maybe in the Lean file, this would correspond to a docstring'. R7 verified that docstrings show in Lean hovers and through findDocString?. python3 is installed for scripts.
issues.suggested_fix: In v0.1, write .telelean/graph.json (format_version 1, the same schema as the planned export) after every refresh, and keep it gitignored; scripts read that file. Defer the providers and the CLI, keeping the core free of `vscode` imports so both are thin wrappers later. Default the docstring mirror to ON for formalized nodes, generated from natural_name, with G5 checking it matches; Lean's own hover then shows the user's sentence at no cost. Replace CodeLens with one 'telelean: Reveal node at cursor' command.

issues.section: §7 Stack and EdgeEngine; 12 npm list (vite, react, zustand, pragmatic-drag-and-drop, shiki)
issues.problem: The UI stack is heavier than v0.1 needs. The custom SVG overlay is genuinely required, but its budget, culling, stub, junction-dot and port-drawn-arrow machinery and its supporting libraries only matter at scale.
issues.evidence: R3's own reference implementation, artifacts/r3-ui-graph/bench/prototype.html (501 lines, vanilla), already has the three columns, edge overlay, stubs, tray, A/D/G switch, diff toggle and native HTML5 drag, and was screenshot-tested in three themes. R3 measured about 1 µs of JS per edge, with about 100 changed paths per frame holding 60 fps and about 300 giving roughly 30 fps, so a budget matters only at hundreds of visible edges. R3 verified that no graph library supports three scrolling viewports with shared edges, so the overlay should stay. R3's reason for React ('most reliable choice for LLM-written code') is fair.
issues.suggested_fix: Keep the custom SVG overlay. React is optional and fine to keep, but bundle both host and webview with esbuild and drop Vite. Use native HTML5 drag and drop instead of pragmatic-drag-and-drop. Show Lean as a plain <pre> with 'Open in editor' instead of Shiki. Redraw all edges per animation frame with endpoints clamped to the column edge. Add the budgeted EdgeEngine, junction dots and port-drawn arrows when node counts or user feedback call for them.

issues.section: D-33 (git snapshot before applying); 03 §6 settings telelean.git.snapshotBeforeApply (true)
issues.problem: By default telelean would commit into the user's own repository, on their current branch, every time they accept a proposal. That is intrusive, and it duplicates the undoable WorkspaceEdit and the shadow workspace's own git history.
issues.evidence: D-33: 'If the model folder is a git repository, telelean also commits a snapshot before applying. This is a setting, and on by default.'
issues.suggested_fix: Default it to off. If it is enabled, store snapshots under a private ref (for example `git stash create` → refs/telelean/snapshots/<run>) so the user's branch and history are untouched.

issues.problem: The rationale policy is inconsistent. A user-typed ASSUMPTION may have no rationale, because walkthrough step 4 (S24) has none. But adopting an agent-proposed ghost assumption requires a self-typed rationale, and the agent's hint 'cannot be submitted unedited'. This is a forcing function the user never asked for.
issues.evidence: D-14: 'This is not blocking, since your walkthrough's 4th assumption has none.' D-6: 'You adopt one only by writing your own rationale; an LLM hint may be shown greyed out but cannot be submitted unedited.' R5's protocol calls the rationale 'mandatory for ASSUMPTIONs'.
issues.suggested_fix: Use one policy everywhere: a rationale is encouraged but never blocking. A ghost can be adopted with an empty rationale, which shows the 'no rationale yet' badge, or with the agent's hint stored with agent provenance (for example `rationale_origin: agent`). Provenance satisfies IC-29, and the user can edit the rationale later.

issues.problem: D-2's deciding argument for `theorem … := by sorry` over the user's own S37 style is that `lake comparator` needs a theorem to compare. If the freeze is deferred (RT-2), that argument disappears. R2 actually recommended the sorry-free statement scheme, which matches the user's `def cynder_not_ ...` example.
issues.evidence: D-2(a): '`lake comparator` needs a theorem to compare'. R2: 'Goals and unproved derivations should be a Prop-valued abbrev (no sorry), with the proof as a separate theorem n.holds'. The t1 report's IC-24 entry says the S37 form 'needs no sorry at all'.
issues.suggested_fix: Present D-2 as a genuine choice. Option (a), theorem plus sorry, is simplest for the agent and propagates sorryAx as a 'conditional' marker. Option (b) is the user's S37 statement-as-def plus a separate proof theorem, with no sorry warnings. Do not use the comparator as the tiebreaker.

issues.problem: The escaping rule in the spec text is wrong: it maps `/-` to `/-`, which is the identity. If implemented as written, a `/-` inside a user's sentence opens a nested Lean comment that swallows the rest of the file.
issues.evidence: Doc 03: '(`-/` as `-\/`, `/-` as `/-`)'. R4's verified rule: in JSON values write `-/` as `-\/` and `/-` as `/-` (writing `\/-` would still contain `/-`); in the Markdown body write `-\/` and `/\-`. R4 verified that a stray `/-` swallows the rest of the file.
issues.suggested_fix: Replace the sentence with R4's rule verbatim, and add a round-trip test that writes a natural_name containing both delimiters and checks that the file still compiles.

issues.section: §8.3 ask_user / propose_formalization ('Blocks until you answer in the board'); §8.4
issues.problem: Questions are held, blocking tool calls. A window reload or extension restart kills the run and the pending question, and the design does not say how a pending question is recovered.
issues.evidence: R1 risk: 'Extension reload, crash or deactivate kills the in-flight query and its pending canUseTool; only defer or persisted sessions can resume.' learnharness needed 10-minute idle timeouts plus transcript replay to cope with held questions (R7).
issues.suggested_fix: Make ask_user non-blocking. It records and renders the questions, then returns 'shown to the user; end your turn now'. The answers arrive as the next user message, over stream-json stdin, or with `--resume <session_id>` after a reload. This removes MCP timeout tuning and lets pending questions survive reloads, in both the CLI and SDK routes.

alternative.name: telelean-lite: walkthrough-first v0.1, a thin harness over Lean and the installed Claude Code CLI
alternative.risks:
1. Automation bias: in a one-shot run the user sees 'proved' while judging the statements. Mitigation: required per-statement ticks, statements listed above proof status, and the Formalize-only path.
2. A one-shot agent can shape brand-new statements toward what it could prove. This is visible in 'You said / Lean says' and partly flagged (zero-assumption proofs, trivial shapes), but for new statements it is human judgement, as with the main design's sign-off.
3. The CLI route relies on documented but unversioned flags and stream-json event shapes (`--restricted`, `--permission-prompts`, HTTP MCP config) of a binary that auto-updates with the Claude Code extension. Mitigation: minimum-version probe, fail closed, and an SDK backend kept possible behind LlmBackend. OAuth under a stripped environment and `--restricted` confinement are unverified in both routes and need a smoke test first.
4. The loopback MCP endpoint opens a local port, mitigated by binding 127.0.0.1 and a per-run bearer token.
5. Without the extractor there are no lemma-level 'derivation used by goal' edges, no type hashes, and no partial facts for files that fail to compile. v0.1 shows declared premises and Lean errors instead.
6. #print axioms has the same kernel-bypass blind spot as collectAxioms, so G0 and leanchecker must stay.
7. Without an edge budget, legibility and frame rate degrade beyond a few hundred changing paths (R3: about 300 changed paths gives roughly 30 fps). The EdgeEngine must be added before models grow large.
8. Pragmatic choices are not yet first-class common-ground records.
9. A vanilla webview accumulates hand-rolled state if it is kept too long; migrate to React or Preact when the UI settles.
alternative.when_to_prefer:
Prefer telelean-lite if the priority is to run the Cynder walkthrough on the user's own subscription soon and to refine the interaction design through real use (switch, columns, question cards, diff overlay) before investing in assurance machinery. It also fits if the user is content to judge formal statements once, in the final diff as S31 describes, and if staying close to the literal spec matters: three kinds, `type:`, a three-position switch, docstrings.

Prefer the main design if the user wants a mechanical statement freeze and an independent back-translation from the very first run, expects large models immediately, or plans to share telelean soon, since sharing needs the API-key and SDK backends. The two are compatible: build telelean-lite first, then add D-18's two-phase mode, the comparator, the extractor, DECISION records, providers and the CLI as increments the user chooses.

questions_for_user: Do you want a smaller first version that runs the Cynder walkthrough end to end, with the extras (statement freeze, back-translation, DECISION records, editor features, CLI) added one by one afterwards? Or would you rather wait for the full v1?

Should telelean drive Claude through your installed Claude Code command line in headless mode (what learnharness does, using the binary you already have), or through the Agent SDK (a proprietary npm package that downloads its own ~330 MB copy of Claude Code)? D-23 currently offers only the SDK.

When the AI finishes, do you want to review the Lean statements and proofs together in one diff, as in your step 7? Or should it stop after writing the statements, wait for your sign-off, and only then prove?
Should the field stay `type:`, as in your sketch, or be renamed to `kind:`?

Should your answers to the AI's questions become `kind: DECISION` blocks in your Lean files (a fifth kind of node)? Or should they stay in session logs until you decide? This is currently a default, not one of the questions you were asked.

For vocabulary the AI creates, like `structure Cynder` or `isCharacter`: should that be its own markup kind (DEFINITION), or Assumptions-column items that telelean recognises as vocabulary from the Lean code?
For free-form requests to the AI, do you want a fourth switch position ('Instruct'), or a separate chat box next to your three-position switch?

Your sketches (smoking.lean, cynder.lean) model concepts as concrete records and inductives, like `Character { past: "dark" }`. Should the AI default to that style, or to uninterpreted axioms (D-4), asking you each time?
May telelean make git commits in your model folder automatically, or should snapshots stay out of your branch history?
Do you need graph analysis while VS Code is closed, which would require a CLI? Or is a JSON snapshot that the extension writes on every refresh enough for now?

Before implementation, may I use a little of your Claude quota on a one-line headless smoke test? It would confirm that your subscription login works with API-key variables stripped and with file access confined to a scratch folder. Neither Claude route has been tried yet.
strengths: Exceptional traceability: all S1–S55 sentences map to requirements and to implied constraints, with honest verified, documented and inferred labels. The three documents and their ★ marks make it easy for the user to override decisions.

It caught, with a kernel-checked countermodel, that the walkthrough's three assumptions do not entail the goal. It then made insufficiency a first-class result with ghost assumptions, never silent axioms. This honours S7 and S28 and the pragmatics that S30 asks the LLM to surface.

D-5's strict reading of the button is exactly the literal meaning of S28. Global axioms make the assumption footprint of each result available from Lean itself (#print axioms or collectAxioms), and promoting or demoting a node becomes a one-line edit.

Security realism backed by experiments. It verified that elaborating Lean runs arbitrary code, contained it with bwrap, sanitizes the snap environment for child processes, never uses --bare, and strips API keys so the subscription is used.

Concrete hazards were found and designed out, each verified: YAML mangling natural language, autoImplicit turning typos into quantified variables, definitional smuggling of assumptions, native_decide auxiliary axioms, and skipKernelTC bypassing #print axioms.
Adding a node writes the user's verbatim words with no LLM involved. This matches the walkthrough and avoids paraphrasing the user's words before formalisation starts.
The 'LSP: not now' answer is correct and well argued, citing Argdown's layering and the fact that scripts want whole-graph snapshots.

UI research: it established that no graph library supports three independently scrolling columns with shared edges, measured SVG repaint costs, and produced a working vanilla prototype screenshot-tested in three themes.
RAM discipline throughout: one Lean job at a time, Mathlib off, memory caps on the sandbox, and an explicit resource budget.
